title: Pages — the shell, round 6: framed panel, quieter Back, Edit in the library

steps.path: The right end of the band above an open page
steps.headline: Back to chat now sits in the same quiet inset pill as the window buttons, with no outline; the pencil is gone.
steps.changed: The bordered pill became the window buttons' own style: an inset pill, muted text that brightens on hover, the Esc key as small muted text. Edit left the band altogether.
steps.notice: Nothing on the band has an outline any more. The band is: panel toggle, page name, Back to chat, window buttons.

steps.path: The panel on the left of an open page
steps.headline: The panel sits in its own rounded container, like the files and games pane in a chat, and Manage pages fills its width.
steps.changed: The panel is a rounded pane on the chrome, inset by the frame edge like the page pane beside it. Manage pages is a full-width pill at its bottom.
steps.notice: Two panes side by side, the same shape; the panel reads as a thing you can hide, not as part of the wall.

steps.path: Top bar → Pages, the top-right corner of each card
steps.headline: Edit in chat lives only on the library cards now, as a pencil beside the pin, with a hover tip.
steps.changed: Each card gains a pencil button before its pin. It is the one place a page is edited from; the page view has no edit control.
steps.notice: To change a page: Manage pages, then the pencil on its card. To pin it: the pin on the card or in the panel.
steps.risk: Editing takes one more step than it did with a button on the page itself.
